plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem topped by a showy flower head of golden ray florets surrounding a dark disk of tiny fertile florets. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky. It is widely grown for seed, oil, and ornament, and also grows wild in prairies and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America native; cultivated across Europe, Ukraine, Russia, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of up to 2,000 tiny florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: A low, evergreen shrub with tiny scale-like leaves and spikes of small bell-shaped flowers that carpet moorlands and heathlands in purple. It thrives in acidic, nutrient-poor soils and is a vital nectar source for bees in late summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Scotland, Northern England, Ireland, Scandinavia, and heathlands across Europe and parts of Asia
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its jelly-like thixotropic texture, which means it must be stirred or pressed to extract rather than spun out.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower forming dense colonies, with arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads atop leafy stems. It is a late-season magnet for butterflies, native bees, and other pollinators, and thrives in meadows, fields, and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (July to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often wrongly blamed for hay fever; the real culprit is usually ragweed, whose wind-borne pollen blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a dense center of flowers surrounded by showy, pointed bracts that resemble petals. It is adapted to nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos habitats and is a popular cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August to November), with some blooming earlier in late winter
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape of South Africa; national flower of South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are an ancient plant family that predates the breakup of Gondwana, with fossils dating back around 300 million years.
